title: AML training requirements by country: Australia, the EU and Portugal, the US, Japan and the UAE compared
description: How AML/CFT training duties compare across Australia, Portugal and the EU, the United States, Japan and the UAE, and what a multinational can standardize.
shortAnswer: Every one of the five markets requires or expects anti-money laundering (AML) training, but the legal force differs. Australia, Portugal, the United States and the UAE impose a binding training duty on regulated businesses, and the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation will do so directly from July 10, 2027. Japan's statute sets only an effort duty, with binding detail for financial institutions coming from Financial Services Agency guidelines. None of the five sets a refresher interval in national law.
keyTakeaways: All five markets expect training that fits each person's role and the money laundering risks of that role; generic, one size courses are criticized by regulators in several of them.

Only Portugal ties the training duty to a retention period for training records in the same law (seven years); UAE federal rules set five years for records generally, and ADGM six years for AML training records.
Japan is the outlier: Article 11 of the Act on Prevention of Transfer of Criminal Proceeds is an effort duty, and the enforceable expectations sit in FSA Guidelines section III-5.
No market sets a refresher interval in national law. Annual cycles come from regulator guidance (AUSTRAC, the Central Bank of the UAE) or, in the ADGM free zone, from the regulator's rulebook.
A multinational can run one global AML curriculum and evidence model, then localize triggers, reporting procedures, thresholds and record periods per market.

sections.heading: How do AML training duties compare across the five markets?

blocks.text: The duties compare closely on substance and differ on legal form, frequency and evidence. Each market requires training for people in roles relevant to anti-money laundering and counter terrorist financing (AML/CFT), tailored to their function, but only some state how often to train or what records to keep. The table summarizes the position as at November 2026, drawing only on the regulation pages linked in each row.

sections.heading: Where is AML training a hard legal duty, and where is it softer?

blocks.text: AML training is a binding legal duty in Australia, Portugal, the United States and the UAE, and will be one under directly applicable EU law from July 10, 2027. Japan is the exception: the statute asks businesses only to endeavor to train employees.

In Australia, training is a required element of an AML/CTF policy under section 26F(4)(e) of the reformed Act, with detail in section 5-9 of the 2025 Rules ([AUSTRAC AML/CTF training](/regulations/austrac-aml-ctf-training-requirements)). In the United States, 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) lists "an ongoing employee training program" as one of four statutory program pillars ([Bank Secrecy Act training](/regulations/bsa-aml-training-requirements)), and each sector rule restates it, for example 31 CFR 1022.210(d)(3) for [money services businesses](/regulations/fincen-msb-aml-program-training). Portugal's Article 55 makes the duty enforceable, and breach is a particularly serious administrative offense with base fines of up to EUR 5,000,000 for credit and financial institutions ([Portugal Law 83/2017](/regulations/portugal-aml-law-training-requirements)). The UAE places the duty in Article 21(5) of Cabinet Resolution No. 134 of 2025 ([UAE AML/CFT training](/regulations/uae-aml-cft-training-requirements)).

Japan's Article 11 item 1 is an effort duty (doryoku gimu), and Article 11 is not among the provisions whose breach can trigger a correction order under Article 18. For FSA supervised financial institutions, however, section III-5 of the FSA Guidelines turns training into five required actions, and the FSA has checked effectiveness verification through inspections since the 2025 program year ([Japan FSA AML/CFT guidelines](/regulations/japan-fsa-aml-cft-guidelines-training)). In practice a Japanese bank faces expectations as demanding as anywhere else; a non financial specified business operator faces far less.

sections.heading: Does any market set a fixed AML refresher interval?

blocks.text: No market fixes a refresher interval in national law, although the ADGM free zone's rulebook does. The words used are "ongoing" (Australia, the EU, the United States), "regular" (Portugal), "periodic" (the UAE) and "continuous" competence checks (Japan).

Annual cycles come from guidance. AUSTRAC offers 6 to 12 months for compliance officers and senior management and 12 months for customer facing staff, but describes these as examples only. The Central Bank of the UAE's best practices on role based training expect an annual training needs assessment, a board approved annual training plan and board training at least annually; the CBUAE states these best practices are not additional regulation. The 2026 US interagency proposal ties frequency to risk profile and role, but is not final ([NCUA credit union BSA training](/regulations/ncua-credit-union-bsa-training)). Portugal is the only market that names a trigger in national law: training immediately after hiring for people whose roles directly concern AML/CFT.

In the UAE's financial free zones, ADGM rule AML 13.2.1 requires AML and targeted financial sanctions training for all employees at least annually ([ADGM FSRA](/regulations/adgm-fsra-training-and-competence)), and DFSA rule AML 12.1.1 requires training at appropriate and regular intervals ([DFSA](/regulations/dfsa-training-and-competence-requirements)).

sections.heading: What training evidence does each regulator expect?

blocks.text: Every regulator expects proof that training happened, and several now expect proof that it worked. The common core is a training plan or policy, completion records by person, and some test of understanding.

items: **Australia:** a training plan, a completion register, effectiveness monitoring and knowledge checks; AUSTRAC says its own e-learning cannot be relied on alone, and its real estate guidance gives a poor practice example of generic vendor training with no completion tracking.

**EU:** a training policy approved by the management body under Article 9(2)(a)(x), and training programs that are "duly documented" under Article 12 ([EU AMLR](/regulations/eu-amlr-training-requirements)).

**Portugal:** complete, up to date training records retained for seven years and available to sectoral authorities; Banco de Portugal Notice 1/2022 Article 53 lists minimum record fields for supervised financial entities.
**United States:** examiners using the FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual look for role based training, board training, and records of dates, materials, attendance and follow up on missed training.

**Japan:** evidence that training is effective, not only delivered; the FSA FAQ also expects training to be updated when national risk assessment or FATF material changes, with checks on those already trained.

**UAE:** documented training plans owned by the compliance officer under Article 22(4), and, for CBUAE licensees, attendance records and post training assessments; ADGM firms record dates, content and attendee names and keep them at least six years.

sections.heading: What should a multinational standardize and what should it localize?

blocks.text: A multinational should standardize its AML training architecture and evidence model, and localize legal triggers, reporting mechanics and record periods. The substance regulators ask for (role and risk tailoring, understanding checks, documented completion) is consistent enough to build once.

blocks.text: The safest default is to meet the strictest version of each element everywhere where that costs little, for example keeping the Portuguese minimum record fields for every market, and to localize only where the law points in a different direction. A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) built on the shared role taxonomy makes the local overlays visible, and [mapping training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) keeps each local rule traceable to a module and an assessment.

sections.heading: Which AML training rules are changing?

blocks.text: Three markets are mid transition as at November 2026. Programs designed now should anticipate them rather than be rebuilt later.

items: **EU and Portugal:** the AMLR applies from July 10, 2027 and sets the training duty directly, so Portuguese entities will work under both Article 12 of the AMLR and the national framework that implements it.

**United States:** FinCEN and the banking agencies proposed new AML/CFT program rules on April 10, 2026, describing the training change as clarifying, not substantive. The current rules apply until a final rule takes effect.

**Australia:** existing reporting entities moved to the reformed obligations on March 31, 2026 and newly regulated professions on July 1, 2026; see the pages on [lawyers and accountants](/regulations/aml-ctf-tranche-2-lawyers-accountants-training) and [real estate](/regulations/aml-ctf-tranche-2-real-estate-training).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each market's AML obligations as a framework of concepts, roles and assessment points before any content is written, so the shared core and the local overlays are explicit. Each assessment item traces back to the obligation it evidences, which supports the record schema regulators in all five markets expect. See [audit evidence](/platform/audit-evidence).

faqs.q: Can one global AML e-learning course satisfy all five regulators?
faqs.a: Not on its own. Every market expects training tailored to role and risk, and AUSTRAC states that its own e-learning cannot be relied on alone. A global course can carry the shared core, but each market needs local reporting procedures, thresholds and role specific content layered on top.

faqs.q: Does the EU AMLR replace Portugal's Law 83/2017 training duty?
faqs.a: From July 10, 2027 the AMLR applies directly in every Member State, including Portugal, so Article 12 sets the training duty without transposition. Portuguese entities should expect national rules to be aligned with it; until then, Article 55 of Law 83/2017 governs.

faqs.q: Is AML training mandatory in Japan?
faqs.a: The statute sets an effort duty only: Article 11 of the Act on Prevention of Transfer of Criminal Proceeds asks businesses to endeavor to train employees. For FSA supervised financial institutions, the FSA Guidelines list required actions on training and the FSA checks their effectiveness in inspections.

faqs.q: How long should AML training records be kept?
faqs.a: It depends on the market. Portugal sets seven years for training records under Article 51 of Law 83/2017, and the UAE sets five years for records under Article 25 of Cabinet Resolution No. 134 of 2025. A group standard often keeps the longest applicable period.
